sources.summary: Public version of the ecological EIA report form (cover: builder 韶关市万国云耀数据科技有限公司, compiled September 2026) for the 万国数据韶关220千伏输变电工程 in Baitu town (Qujiang) and Longgui town (Wujiang), Shaoguan. It states that the GDS Shaoguan computing cluster (韶关万国数据算力集群) needs large amounts of electricity, so the company is investing in a new 220 kV substation, GDS I (220kV万国I站), with a double-circuit line to the 220 kV Tanjie station (about 11.5 km) and a 2.3 km cable to the planned 220 kV Baitu data-centre station; its supply range is the GDS Shaoguan computing cluster. It describes the GDS data centre as a core data carrier of Shaoguan to be built with GDS's latest T-BLOCK prefabricated modules. The substation project was approved by the Shaoguan DRC in June 2026 (韶发改电力〔2026〕6号, project code 2603-440200-04-01-662978; total investment CNY 325.16 million). Phase 1 (2x120 MVA, maximum load 112.6 MW) is planned to enter service in December 2026; phase 2 (4x140 MVA, a further 112.8 MW, 225.4 MW in total) is planned for December 2027 (page 30) or April 2028 (page 29), an inconsistency in the filing. It prints the proposed substation centre as 113°30′33.452″, 24°41′11.126″. These are substation plans and grid load figures, not data-centre IT capacity; the filing does not report data-centre construction, completion or operation.
sources.date_semantics: Published as the attachment of the Shaoguan Ecology and Environment Bureau acceptance notice dated 2026-10-26 (page PubDate 2026-10-26 09:06:05; acceptance date 2026-10-23). sources.title: Village of Itasca Village Board agenda packet, 15 September 2026 (first reading of Res. 1734-26, development agreement with NTT Global Data for the CH4 data center building; staff memo submitted 13 August 2026)
sources.summary: The packet's Community Development memo (from the Community Development Director to the Village Administrator, submitted 13 August 2026, first reading 15 September 2026) recommends a development agreement with NTT Global Data for the CH4 data center building at the north-west corner of Pierce Road and North Arlington Heights Road. Its background and discussion say that the Village Board's Ordinance 2081-23 (5 September 2023) granted zoning entitlements for a data center, electrical substation and related improvements on NTT Global Data Centers, LLC's property at the intersection of Pierce Road and Hamilton Lakes Drive (CH3); that a December 2024 letter of understanding (Res. 1588-24) let the CH3 and CH4 projects start before a development agreement; that 'The petitioner, NTT Global Data Centers CH, LLC, has developed two buildings to date, CH1 and CH2. CH3, a new 270,000-square-foot Data Center, is currently under construction. An electric substation has also been approved and is under construction'; that the campus at the Hamilton Lakes Regional Office Center was planned in three phases, with CH1 opened in 2020, CH2 started in 2022 and 'the third phase CH3 Data Center is currently under construction', while 'CH4 and CH5 have received entitlement approvals and are actively seeking permits'; and that the campus is divided into four lots (Lot 1, PIN 03-05-200-042, substation; Lot 2, completed CH1 and CH2; Lot 4, PINs 03-05-200-019, -020 and -029, CH4), with four data-center buildings and one substation on the 35-acre campus when complete. The attached agreement (effective 27 August 2026) names NTT Global Data Centers CH4, LLC as owner and developer of about 12.2 acres at 1200 and 1250 Arlington Heights Road under Ordinance 2119-24. The packet's finance report (as of 31 July 2026) says building permit fees were paid for 'NTT CH2 (275 Pierce)' and a mass grading permit for 'NTT CH4 (1200 N. Arlington Heights)'.
sources.date_semantics: Agenda packet for the Village Board meeting of 15 September 2026, filed in the Village's Agenda Center under 09152026; the PDF carries no embedded date, so the printed meeting date is used as the publication date. The CH3 statement is in a staff memo marked 'SUBMITTED: August 13, 2026', so the under-construction observation is dated 13 August 2026 (the date of the statement), not the start of construction or an inspection day.
sources.personal_data_note: The memo and agreement name Village staff and give notice contacts; no personal names, telephone numbers or e-mail addresses are copied.

sources.title: TierPoint: Oklahoma City Data Centers page (OKC and OK2; version modified 3 September 2026)
sources.summary: TierPoint's Oklahoma City page says that 'TierPoint operates two state-of-the-art data centers' in Oklahoma City, that 'TierPoint is the largest commercial data center provider in Oklahoma' and that 'These two TierPoint state-of-the-art Oklahoma City data center facilities are interconnected via multiple private fiber paths'. It gives separate facility specifications for 4121 Perimeter Center Place (22,000+ total square feet, 14,000+ square feet of raised floor, cabinets and cages available, three 1 MW redundant generators) and 4114 Perimeter Center Place (69,000+ total square feet, 34,000+ square feet of raised floor, cabinets and cages available, two 2 MW redundant generators), each with A-side and B-side power distribution, a 100% uptime SLA, carrier-neutral connectivity, 24x7x365 security, managed services and remote hands, and annual SOC 1/SOC 2, HITRUST, HIPAA and PCI-DSS audits, and lists 'Oklahoma City (OKC, OK2) 4121 Perimeter Center Place ... 4114 Perimeter Center Place, Oklahoma City, OK 73112'. Its structured data define two LocalBusiness entries: 'TierPoint Oklahoma City Data Center (OKC)' at 4121 Perimeter Center Place with GeoCoordinates 35.514391, -97.596607, and 'TierPoint Oklahoma City Data Center (OK2)' at 4114 Perimeter Center Place with GeoCoordinates 35.514094, -97.595073. These present-tense statements describe two facilities in service.

sources.summary: DataBank's own news item, written by DataBank about NY1's coverage, says that NY1 'reports on community opposition surrounding DataBank's existing facility and proposed expansion in Orangeburg, Rockland County'. It calls the expansion 'DataBank's 45-megawatt Orangeburg campus project' and says it falls outside the 50 MW threshold of the Governor's executive moratorium. It also says 'The town of Orangetown passed its own moratorium this week but exempted the DataBank project because it is already in the approval process'. DataBank's senior vice president of marketing is quoted saying that the facility uses closed-loop cooling and draws no water from Lake Tappan. These DataBank statements identify a proposed, not yet approved expansion of the Orangeburg campus as of the item's publication. The 45 MW is a campus power figure, not IT load, and is not used as a capacity.

sources.title: Homer City Generation: Homer City Generation Highlights Kiewit's One-Year Anniversary of Being Active On Site as Engineering, Procurement, and Construction Partner (release, 20 October 2026)
sources.summary: Homer City Generation, L.P. announces that October 2026 marks one year since Kiewit Power Constructors Co. began work on the Homer City Energy Campus as the project's EPC partner. It says that 'over the past year, Kiewit has led demolition and construction on the 3,200-acre site while building a workforce of more than 2,000 skilled tradespeople and contractors'. It also says that Kiewit 'began vertical construction on the site in April 2026 with the first structure to rise on the campus' and completed demolition and excavation in June 2026. More recently, it says, Kiewit oversaw the installation of the first two heat recovery steam generators (transported to the campus from September 2026) and the setting of the first gas turbine on its foundation. A Kiewit project director quoted in the release looks forward to 'carrying that momentum through construction'. These statements report construction in progress on the campus on the release date. The work described is site, demolition and power-generation construction. The release does not state that data-centre buildings are under construction, complete or operating. Named individuals quoted in the release are not recorded.
